assembly_instructions: Open microarchitecture block diagram, no chassis. Scale 1x (the pipeline is treated as a ~14 m logical board so bounds.radius stays near 7.6). +X is the instruction-flow direction; the six in-order stages sit on the ground line (z=0) left-to-right: PC generation, instruction fetch, decode, issue, execute, commit. Five tall translucent glass plates straddle z=0 between consecutive stages — these are the pipeline registers. Front-end support (BHT/BTB/RAS predictors tied to PC-gen by a Z-running prediction bus, L1 I$, instruction queue, I-TLB) is placed on the -Z side near fetch; the compressed-instruction decoder sits on -Z by decode; the scoreboard sits on -Z by issue; the register file — split into a stacked integer bank and floating-point bank — sits on +Z by issue. The six functional units fed by the issue stage form a 2x3 grid on the +Z side behind execute: ALU/branch/CSR on the near row, multiplier/FPU/LSU on the far row. The LSU's store buffer, L1 D$ and D-TLB cluster around the LSU. The hardware page-table walker sits deep on -Z and bridges both TLBs: a copper bus runs to the I-TLB, and a two-segment L-routed copper bus runs east then up the data column to the D-TLB. Behind the walker the AXI4 main-memory interface forms the memory-side boundary, and external DRAM (main memory) sits behind the AXI interface, closing the hierarchy. Copper cylinders are the buses: five backbone buses thread the pipeline through the register plates, a Z-running dispatch bus feeds the functional units, a Z-running writeback bus returns their results to commit, and short copper stubs link the caches, the predictors, the PTW, the AXI interface and DRAM.

info.summary: CVA6 is an open-source 6-stage, single-issue, in-order 64-bit RISC-V application-class core (RV64GC) capable of booting Linux. It was created at ETH Zurich/University of Bologna as 'Ariane' and is now maintained by the OpenHW Group.
info.description: CVA6 implements the RV64GC instruction set with M/S/U privilege modes and a full memory-management unit, making it one of the smallest fully Linux-capable open-source cores. Its six-stage in-order pipeline — PC generation, instruction fetch, decode, issue, execute, commit — buffers instructions in an instruction queue after fetch so the front-end and back-end decouple. The issue stage is built around a scoreboard that tracks in-flight instructions and dispatches them to six functional units (ALU, branch unit, CSR unit, integer multiplier, FPU, and a load-store unit with a store buffer), then commits results strictly in program order from the 64-entry register file.
info.contractor: ETH Zurich & University of Bologna (PULP Platform)
info.contract_value: Open source (Solderpad Hardware License, no cost)

facts.label: MMU
facts.value: Separate I/D TLBs + hardware page-table walker (Sv39)

facts.label: Branch prediction
facts.value: Branch history table, branch target buffer, return stack

facts.label: Memory interface
facts.value: AXI4, separate instruction and data ports

sources.title: Zaruba & Benini, 'The Cost of Application-Class Processing' (IEEE TVLSI 2019)

parts.name: PC Generation Stage
parts.role: Computes the next program counter, applying branch predictions to steer the front-end.

parts.name: Branch History Table
parts.role: Records taken/not-taken history so PC generation can predict conditional branch direction.

parts.name: Branch Target Buffer
parts.role: Caches predicted target addresses of branches and jumps for the PC generation stage.

parts.name: Return Address Stack
parts.role: Pushes return addresses on calls and pops them on returns so PC generation predicts function-return targets.

parts.name: Branch-Prediction Bus
parts.role: Carries direction, target and return-address predictions from the BHT, BTB and RAS into PC generation.

parts.name: PC/Fetch Pipeline Register
parts.role: Latches the program counter between PC generation and instruction fetch.

parts.name: PC-to-Fetch Bus
parts.role: Carries the resolved program counter from PC generation into the fetch stage.

parts.name: Instruction Fetch Stage
parts.role: Reads instruction words from the L1 instruction cache and pushes them into the instruction queue.

parts.name: L1 Instruction Cache
parts.role: 16 KiB cache supplying instruction words to the fetch stage at low latency.

parts.name: I-Cache Refill Bus
parts.role: Connects the fetch stage to the L1 instruction cache for instruction reads and refills.

parts.name: Instruction Queue
parts.role: Buffers fetched instructions in a FIFO, decoupling the front-end from the in-order back-end.

parts.name: Instruction TLB
parts.role: Translates instruction virtual addresses to physical addresses for the fetch path.

parts.name: Fetch/Decode Pipeline Register
parts.role: Latches fetched instruction words between fetch and decode.

parts.name: Fetch-to-Decode Bus
parts.role: Carries raw instruction words from the fetch stage to the decoder.

parts.name: Decode Stage
parts.role: Expands instruction words into the internal micro-op format with source/destination operand fields.

parts.name: Compressed Instruction Decoder
parts.role: Expands 16-bit RV64C compressed instructions into their 32-bit equivalents before main decoding.

parts.name: Decode/Issue Pipeline Register
parts.role: Latches decoded micro-ops between decode and issue.

parts.name: Decode-to-Issue Bus
parts.role: Carries decoded micro-ops from the decoder into the issue stage.

parts.name: Issue Stage
parts.role: Reads operands, tracks dependencies via the scoreboard, and dispatches micro-ops to functional units.

parts.name: Scoreboard
parts.role: Tracks every in-flight instruction and its pending result to enforce data hazards and in-order commit.

parts.name: Register File — Integer Bank
parts.role: Holds the 32 architectural 64-bit integer registers, read at issue and written back in order at commit.

parts.name: Register File — Floating-Point Bank
parts.role: Holds the 32 architectural 64-bit floating-point registers of the F/D extensions, stacked above the integer bank.

parts.name: Dispatch Bus
parts.role: Fans micro-ops and operands from the issue stage out to all six functional units.

parts.name: Issue/Execute Pipeline Register
parts.role: Latches dispatched operations between issue and execute.

parts.name: Issue-to-Execute Bus
parts.role: Carries dispatched operations from the issue stage into the execute stage.

parts.name: Execute Stage
parts.role: Sequences operations through the functional units and gathers their results for commit.

parts.name: ALU
parts.role: Performs single-cycle integer arithmetic, logic and shift operations.

parts.name: Branch Unit
parts.role: Resolves branches and jumps, signalling mispredictions back to the front-end.

parts.name: CSR Unit
parts.role: Reads and writes control and status registers for the M/S/U privilege modes.

parts.name: Integer Multiplier / Divider
parts.role: Executes multi-cycle integer multiply and divide operations of the M extension.

parts.name: Floating-Point Unit
parts.role: Executes IEEE-754 single and double precision floating-point operations (F/D extensions).

parts.name: Load-Store Unit
parts.role: Issues memory accesses, translating addresses through the D-TLB and queuing writes in the store buffer.

parts.name: Store Buffer
parts.role: Holds committed stores in a FIFO until they drain to the data cache, letting the pipeline advance.

parts.name: L1 Data Cache
parts.role: 32 KiB write-back cache serving load and store data to the load-store unit.

parts.name: D-Cache Access Bus
parts.role: Connects the load-store unit to the L1 data cache for load and store traffic.

parts.name: Data TLB
parts.role: Translates data virtual addresses to physical addresses for the load-store unit.

parts.name: Hardware Page-Table Walker
parts.role: Walks Sv39 page tables in memory to refill the instruction and data TLBs on a miss.

parts.name: I-TLB Refill Bus
parts.role: Carries page-table-walk results from the walker into the instruction TLB on a translation miss.

parts.name: D-TLB Refill Bus (memory-side run)
parts.role: Carries page-table-walk results from the walker eastward toward the data-side memory-management cluster.

parts.name: D-TLB Refill Bus (data-side run)
parts.role: Carries page-table-walk results up the data column into the data TLB on a translation miss.

parts.name: PTW Memory-Access Bus
parts.role: Carries page-table-walk memory requests from the walker down to the AXI memory interface.

parts.name: AXI4 Main-Memory Interface
parts.role: Bridges the L1 caches and page-table walker to external DRAM over the AXI4 bus, arbitrating instruction and data traffic.

parts.name: External DRAM (Main Memory)
parts.role: Off-chip DRAM holding instructions, data and page tables, accessed by the core through the AXI4 interface.

parts.name: AXI4 DRAM Bus
parts.role: Carries AXI4 read/write transactions between the memory interface and external DRAM.

parts.name: Execute/Commit Pipeline Register
parts.role: Latches functional-unit results between execute and commit.

parts.name: Execute-to-Commit Bus
parts.role: Carries completed results from the execute stage into the commit stage.

parts.name: Commit Stage
parts.role: Retires instructions strictly in program order, writing results back to the register file.

parts.name: Exception / Trap Controller
parts.role: Detects faults and interrupts at commit and redirects the front-end into the M/S trap handlers.

parts.name: Writeback Bus
parts.role: Returns functional-unit results to the commit stage for in-order retirement.
